summary: Gradual throughput drift in dedicated pool attributed to kernel-queue skew and tenant GPU imbalance
description: Issue summary: LexaSearch (dedicated customer) reports a gradual 10-25% throughput drift over the last 48 hours on their reserved pool. Impact: sustained increase in per-request latency and reduced overall throughput for batched routes; customers observe increased queuing and occasional 5xx spikes under load.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send steady production traffic matching LexaSearch workload shape (median seq len ~512, bursty between 50-200 rps). 2) Target their dedicated pool (pool id: dp-lexa-03). 3) Observe request latencies and per-GPU kernel_queue_wait_ms over 1-3 hour window. 4) Run concurrent heavy tenant (another internal test tenant) to simulate imbalance. Expected: stable throughput near committed TPS; Observed: progressive drop and spikes in kernel queue wait and GPU stall metrics.
logs:
Relevant Grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/lexa/dedicated-pools?panel=kernel_queue_wait_ms (shows drift); pod logs: /var/log/redwood/serving/dp-lexa-03/2026-03-12.log snippets show repeated 'kvcache-miss -> load-next' and 'kernel_queue_delay' warnings; kube events show periodic 'EvictionPredicted' signals around 2026-03-12T22:00Z. Example log excerpt: 
  - 2026-03-12T21:58:07Z svc[worker-4]: kernel_queue_delay=42ms gpu_util=78% kvcache_hit=0.71 
  - 2026-03-12T22:05:31Z svc[worker-4]: kernel_queue_delay=380ms gpu_util=95% kvcache_hit=0.42 
  - 2026-03-13T00:12:02Z svc[orch]: scale_down_attempt blocked_by_kernel_queue=true
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reported throughput drop on 2026-03-10 after an increase in peak traffic. Provided initial traces and asked for SRE assistance; ticket escalated.

SRE (Marco): Confirmed drift on Grafana. Observed correlated increase in kernel_queue_wait_ms and uneven GPU utilization across nodes in the pool. Opening traceroute to check inter-node latency—no network anomalies found.

Customer (LexaSearch): We see increasing tail latency and more frequent 429s from our app logs when bursts occur. No config changes on our side. We rely on the reserved pool for steady batch inference.

SRE (Marco): Ran internal hammer test against dp-lexa-03 and an adjacent noisy test tenant. When the noisy tenant runs heavy KV-cache-unfriendly workloads, kernel queue wait on LexaSearch workers increases by ~3-5x. Suspect scheduler imbalance and kernel-level batching skew.

Eng (Rina Chen): Noted similar symptoms in INT-4321; possible root cause in recent scheduler commit that changed placement heuristics for model-variant affinity. Posting a draft patch for fairness heuristics: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/9876

Support (Aisha): Shared temporary mitigation with customer: applied per-tenant rate-bound and bumped burst buffer to reduce cross-tenant preemption. Requested permission to drain and reprovision two nodes for rebalancing.
Customer (LexaSearch): Approved node drain and agreed to a brief maintenance window 2026-03-13T02:00Z-02:30Z UTC. Asked for timeline to permanent fix.

SRE (Marco): Drained two nodes, observed immediate 12% throughput recovery for LexaSearch after rebalancing. However, kernel_queue_wait_ms baseline remained elevated by ~10% in some pods — further changes required.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: (1) Scheduler placement changed recently causing hot-tenancy—multiple high-throughput slices landed on same GPU families leading to kernel queue saturation; (2) Kernel batching heuristics cause long tail when mix of long/short sequences under same worker; (3) KV cache miss patterns from noisy tenant cause repeated CPU->GPU stalls. Evidence: Grafana shows skewed GPU utilization: some GPUs at 95% with kernel_queue_wait spikes, others at 45%. Related telemetry: batch_size distribution shifted towards higher variance after 2026-03-09 deploy. Correlated PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/commit/1a2b3c4 (placement heuristics). Related runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Dedicated+pool+rebalancing+runbook. Actions taken: node drain/reprovision, applied per-tenant soft-rate limiter, captured perf traces (perf traces uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-support/sup-77109/traces/). Next steps: roll back placement heuristic in staging, add kernel-queue watermark based autoscaler gate, and add tenant fairness scoring to scheduler algorithm.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied 2026-03-13: rebalanced pool by draining two GPUs and reprovisioning on different racks; applied per-tenant soft rate limits to noisy neighbor; reverted placement-affinity change in staging for validation. Immediate customer impact: throughput recovered ~12% post-drain and tail latencies improved. Long-term fix: scheduled scheduler fairness patch and autoscaler gate to prevent scale-down when kernel_queue_wait_ms above threshold. Planned production rollout: canary 2026-03-16, full rollout 2026-03-18 contingent on canary metrics.
follow_up_tasks: ENG: implement tenant fairness scoring (PR open) - assigned to Rina Chen
SRE: add kernel_queue_wait_ms alarm to dedicated pools - assigned to Marco Silva
DOC: update runbook for drain/reprovision steps - assigned to Support lead
closure_notes: Ticket remains open while long-term fixes are tested in staging. Customer will be notified of canary results and timeline. If canary shows no regressions, we'll schedule full rollout and close the ticket.
